title: Services, HTTP, and route guards
summary: Move the cart request into a root-provided service and keep failures visible to the caller.

scenario.briefing: The cart summary renders an empty list on every failure, so the page cannot tell a full cart from a broken request. Move the HTTP boundary into an injected service, let the error propagate, and keep manual subscriptions out of the component.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Add a constructor parameter typed HttpClient and mark it private readonly.
Delete the of([]) fallback so a failed request stays visible to the caller.

misconceptions.description: Returning an empty array when the request fails.
misconceptions.feedback: An empty array is a valid cart, so the caller can no longer tell success from failure. Let the error reach the caller and render an error state.
misconceptions.testDescription: The request is typed and returned without a silent fallback.

misconceptions.description: Constructing the service with new instead of injecting it.
misconceptions.feedback: The service needs HttpClient and application scope. Inject it through the constructor or inject().
misconceptions.diagnostic: Calling new CartService() skips HttpClient and the application injector.

misconceptions.description: Subscribing to the observable inside the service.
misconceptions.feedback: A service that subscribes takes ownership of the request and the cleanup. Return the observable and let the consumer decide when to subscribe.

sections.title: Root-provided services share one instance
sections.body: An @Injectable({ providedIn: "root" }) service is created once for the application injector. Any component or guard that asks for it receives the same instance, so cart state and HTTP access stay in one place.

sections.title: Constructor injection names the dependency
sections.body: The constructor declares what the service needs. Angular reads the parameter types and supplies HttpClient, which the application provides through provideHttpClient(). Calling new CartService() would skip that wiring.

sections.title: HTTP observables are cold and failures are values
sections.body: HttpClient methods return observables that start the request when subscribed. Return the observable unchanged so the caller can render an error state; catching the error and returning an empty array hides a broken request.

sections.title: Guards run before the route activates
sections.body: A functional guard uses inject(CartService) and returns true, false, or a UrlTree that redirects. It runs before the routed component is created, so it can block a cart page for a visitor without a session.

sections.title: The production build is its own target
sections.body: ng build compiles ahead of time, checks template types, applies bundle budgets, and writes hashed files. A budget or template error fails the build; fixing it is part of the work, not a reason to ship the development bundle.

vocabulary.definition: A decorator that marks a class as available to Angular's dependency injector.
Declaring dependencies as constructor parameters so the injector supplies them.
A route guard written as a function that can inject services and return a decision.
Compiling templates during the build so template errors surface before the browser runs.

steps.title: Expose the cart through an injectable service
steps.prompt: Edit cart.service.ts. Make the service application-wide, receive HttpClient through its constructor, and return a typed cart request that lets failures reach the caller.

tests.description: The service is provided once at the application root.
The request is typed and returned without a silent fallback.

hints: Remove of([]) and catchError so failures reach the caller.

localVerification.description: Run the Angular unit tests with the Angular CLI.

steps.title: Review the cart subscription
steps.prompt: Review cart-summary.component.ts and select every real problem.

artifact.title: cart-summary.component.ts
artifact.caption: The summary subscribes by hand, hides request failures, and uses NgFor without importing it.

findings.label: The subscription in ngOnInit is never unsubscribed.
The error handler replaces a failed request with an empty cart.
The standalone component uses *ngFor without importing CommonModule or NgFor.
The component must list CartService in providers because the service is root-provided.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the subscription, error state, and template import are fixed.
Ship it; the cart summary is short-lived.

steps.explanation: The manual subscription keeps running after the component is destroyed, and the error callback makes a failed request look like an empty cart. The standalone template also cannot resolve *ngFor without importing CommonModule or NgFor. Return the observable to the template or unsubscribe in ngOnDestroy, and surface the failure.
hints: Check whether the subscription has a lifetime bound to the component.
Look at what the error callback does with a failed request.
Check the standalone template imports for *ngFor.
Ignore the false finding about providers and block on the real risks.
